brief: A base with a bay bin in one half of its cell.

requirements.requirement: A base (hex base cell) is present
requirements.evidence: piece:0,0,0 as a Hex base · East half (half-e variant), replacing the original Full base.

requirements.requirement: A bin sits in one half of the base's cell
requirements.evidence: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-half-e-full (Bin, east half, full depth), cut to the east half outline of the cell. A full-cell bin was refused with FOOTPRINT_MISMATCH against the full base, so the base was changed to half-e to match.

I read 'bay bin' as the half-cell bin. The catalog's 'bay' family (Half/Full bay tray) is a notch that stands in an empty spot beside three cells, not inside a base cell, so I did not use it. If a bay tray was meant, it would need a different layout.
check_build: ok, meshClash clear. Only info: 3 faces could take a cap (open faces, not an error).

finish.summary: The build is one East-half hex base with an east-half, full-depth bin filling that half of the cell. It passes check_build with no errors and a clear mesh check. The main uncertainty is that "bay bin" might have meant the catalog's bay-tray notch, which sits beside three cells rather than in a base cell; I used the half-cell bin instead.
